CREATE TABLE `api_tokens`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `token` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `secret` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `delayed_jobs`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `priority` INT NOT NULL,
    `attempts` INT NOT NULL,
    `handler` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `last_error` TEXT NULL,
    `run_at` DATETIME NULL,
    `locked_at` DATETIME NULL,
    `failed_at` DATETIME NULL,
    `locked_by` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `queue` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NULL
);

CREATE TABLE `email_templates`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `subject` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `content` TEXT NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `history_items`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `item_type` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `item_id` INT NULL,
    `date` DATETIME NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `issue_service_joins`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `issue_id` INT NULL,
    `service_id` INT NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`issue_id`) REFERENCES `issues`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`service_id`) REFERENCES `services`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `issue_updates`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `issue_id` INT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NULL,
    `service_status_id` INT NULL,
    `state` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `text` TEXT NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `identifier` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `notify` TINYINT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`issue_id`) REFERENCES `issues`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`service_status_id`) REFERENCES `service_statuses`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `issues`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `title` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `state` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `service_status_id` INT NULL,
    `all_services` TINYINT NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NULL,
    `identifier` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `notify` TINYINT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`service_status_id`) REFERENCES `service_statuses`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `maintenance_service_joins`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `maintenance_id` INT NULL,
    `service_id` INT NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`service_id`) REFERENCES `services`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`maintenance_id`) REFERENCES `maintenances`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `maintenance_updates`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `maintenance_id` INT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NULL,
    `text` TEXT NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `identifier` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `notify` TINYINT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`maintenance_id`) REFERENCES `maintenances`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `maintenances`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `title` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `description` TEXT NULL,
    `start_at` DATETIME NULL,
    `finish_at` DATETIME NULL,
    `length_in_minutes` INT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NULL,
    `service_status_id` INT NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `closed_at` DATETIME NULL,
    `identifier` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `notify` TINYINT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`service_status_id`) REFERENCES `service_statuses`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `nifty_attachments`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `parent_id` INT NULL,
    `parent_type` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `token` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `digest` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `role` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `file_name` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `file_type` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `schema_migrations`(
    `version` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY
);
CREATE TABLE `service_groups`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `service_statuses`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `permalink` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `color` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `status_type` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `services`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `permalink` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `position` INT NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `status_id` INT NULL,
    `description` TEXT NULL,
    `group_id` INT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `sites`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `title` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `description` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `domain` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `support_email` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `website_url` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `time_zone` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `crawling_permitted` TINYINT NULL,
    `email_from_name` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `email_from_address` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `allow_subscriptions` TINYINT NULL,
    `http_protocol` VARCHAR(255) NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `subscribers`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `email_address` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `verification_token` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `verified_at` DATETIME NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `users`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `email_address` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `password_digest` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `created_at` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `updated_at` DATETIME NOT NULL
);

Background / Context

Staytus is a status page platform developed using Rails. It serves organizations needing to communicate real-time issues and maintenance events to their customers, ensuring transparency for web applications, networks, or services they provide, which are expected to be accessible 24/7. 

Objectives

The primary objective is to create a comprehensive solution that allows organizations to publish and manage the latest information about service issues and maintenance activities, ensuring timely communication with users and stakeholders.

Stakeholders & Users

1. Organizations who need to communicate service status to customers.
2. System Administrators responsible for managing and updating the status information.
3. End Users who rely on the organization's services and subscribe to updates.

Functional Descriptions

1. User Interface
   - Responsive and attractive design for both public and admin views.
   - Customizable themes for branding needs.

2. Issue Tracking
   - Admins can log and update issues as they occur.
   - Continuous posting of updates on existing issues.

3. Maintenance Management
   - Admins can schedule and announce maintenance sessions.
   - Provide real-time updates during maintenance activities.

4. Email Notifications
   - Users can subscribe to service updates via email.
   - Automated notifications for new issues and scheduled maintenance.

5. API Integration
   - JSON API for updating statuses from external systems.
   - Integration capability with existing monitoring solutions.

6. Collaborative Updates
   - Multiple users can update the site to keep information current.

Non-Functional Descriptions

1. Performance
   - Efficient data handling optimized for near real-time updates.

2. Scalability
   - Capable of accommodating a growing number of users and updates.

3. Security
   - Secure access for administrators and sensitive data handling.

4. Reliability
   - Must ensure uptime to provide continuous access to status information.

5. Usability
   - Intuitive and user-friendly interfaces across all devices.

The schemabench_0077 database is used to store data for a web-based issue tracking and maintenance management system. It contains 18 tables, each representing a different entity or relationship in the system.
The api_tokens table stores API tokens used for authentication and authorization. It has six columns: an ID, a name, a token, a secret, a created_at timestamp, and an updated_at timestamp.
The delayed_jobs table stores delayed jobs for the system. It has 11 columns: an ID, a priority, the number of attempts, a handler, a last error, a run_at timestamp, a locked_at timestamp, a failed_at timestamp, a locked_by value, a queue name, a created_at timestamp, and an updated_at timestamp.
The email_templates table stores email templates used for sending notifications. It has five columns: an ID, a name, a subject, a content, and a created_at timestamp.
The history_items table stores historical data for issues and maintenances. It has three columns: an ID, an item_type, and a date.
The issue_service_joins table stores relationships between issues and services. It has four columns: an ID, an issue_id, a service_id, a created_at timestamp, and an updated_at timestamp.
The issue_updates table stores updates to issues. It has 11 columns: an ID, an issue_id, a user_id, a service_status_id, a state, a text, a created_at timestamp, an updated_at timestamp, an identifier, a notify value, and a foreign key referencing the issues table.
The issues table stores information about issues. It has 13 columns: an ID, a title, a state, a service_status_id, an all_services value, a created_at timestamp, an updated_at timestamp, a user_id, an identifier, a notify value, and two foreign keys referencing the service_statuses and users tables.
The maintenance_service_joins table stores relationships between maintenances and services. It has four columns: an ID, a maintenance_id, a service_id, a created_at timestamp, and an updated_at timestamp.
The maintenance_updates table stores updates to maintenances. It has 10 columns: an ID, a maintenance_id, a user_id, a text, a created_at timestamp, an updated_at timestamp, an identifier, a notify value, and two foreign keys referencing the maintenances and users tables.
The maintenances table stores information about maintenances. The nifty_attachments table stores attachments for issues and maintenances. It has nine columns: an ID, a parent_id, a parent_type, a token, a digest, a role, a file_name, a file_type, and two timestamps.
The schema_migrations table stores information about database schema migrations. It has one column: a version.
The service_groups table stores information about service groups. It has four columns: an ID, a name, a created_at timestamp, and an updated_at timestamp.
The service_statuses table stores information about service statuses. It has seven columns: an ID, a name, a permalink, a color, a status_type, a created_at timestamp, and an updated_at timestamp.
The services table stores information about services. It has 12 columns: an ID, a name, a permalink, a position, a created_at timestamp, an updated_at timestamp, a status_id, a description, a group_id, and two foreign keys referencing the service_statuses and service_groups tables.
The sites table stores information about the system's site. It has 13 columns: an ID, a title, a description, a domain, a support_email, a website_url, a time_zone, a crawling_permitted value, an email_from_name, an email_from_address, an allow_subscriptions value, and an http_protocol.
The subscribers table stores information about subscribers. It has six columns: an ID, an email_address, a verification_token, a verified_at timestamp, a created_at timestamp, and an updated_at timestamp.
The users table stores information about users. It has six columns: an ID, an email_address, a name, a password_digest, a created_at timestamp, and an updated_at timestamp.
In summary, the schemabench_0077 database stores data for a web-based issue tracking and maintenance management system, with 18 tables representing different entities and relationships in the system. Each table has its own set of columns, and some tables have foreign keys referencing other tables in the schema.
